newsitem.title: NORWAY: Fokus to announce cost cuts - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Fokus to announce cost cuts - newspaper.

text.p: Fokus Bank, Norway's third largest commercial bank, will announce annual cost cuts of 80 million crowns when it presents 1996 profits on February 6, daily Dagens Naeringsliv said on Monday.

The Dagens Naeringsliv also said it was probably just a matter of time before Fokus Bank may merge with at least one of three regional commercial banks Nordlandsbanken, Bergensbanken and Romsdals Fellesbank.
A Fokus Bank spokeswoman, while confirming that the annual result would be announced on February 6, declined to comment on the report.
The paper also said it was possible that Fokus Bank might be taken over by Sweden's Svenska Handelsbanken, which it said was aiming for a large share of the Norwegian market.
"Since as much as 75 percent of stock in Fokus is foreign-owned, a takeover is not likely to be blocked," the newspaper said.
"All this makes the Fokus share a good buy, although it is now traded at record prices," the Dagens Naeringsliv said. "So far this year the Fokus share has risen by 12 percent to about 49 crowns."
The share was traded at 49.30 crowns on Monday morning, up 1.30 crowns from Friday's close.
The newspaper said the planned cuts would make the bank better positioned to meet a possible further narrowing of profit margins in Norway's overbanked financial industry.
Fokus said in October 1996 that nine-month net profits fell eight percent to 383 million crowns and attributed the weaker result to narrowing interest margins.
Sweeping cost cuts were announced last year by Norway's top commercial banks, Den norske Bank (DnB) and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse.
